name: mindtrail-retrieval-holdout
description: Held-out set written after the default thresholds were fixed on mindtrail-retrieval v1. Different domains (mobile app, data platform, infrastructure). Never used for tuning.

memories.content: The Android app is written in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose for UI
The iOS app uses SwiftUI and targets iOS 17 and later
Crash reports are collected with Sentry; the DSN is injected at build time
App Store builds are uploaded by Fastlane from the release pipeline
Push notifications are sent through Firebase Cloud Messaging
Strings must be added to the Localizable files for English, German and Japanese
Offline data is cached in a local SQLite database via Room on Android
Screenshot tests run with Paparazzi and must be re-recorded after UI changes
The minimum Android SDK level is 26
The minimum Android SDK level was raised to 28
Beta builds are distributed to testers through TestFlight and Firebase App Distribution
The warehouse is Snowflake; transformations are written as dbt models
Pipelines are orchestrated by Airflow DAGs in the dags/ folder
dbt models must have a unique and not_null test on their primary key
Raw events arrive from Segment into the RAW.EVENTS schema
Dashboards for the business team are built in Looker
Personally identifiable columns are masked with a Snowflake masking policy
Run `dbt build --select state:modified+` to test only changed models
The nightly revenue job is owned by the finance analytics team
Ownership of the nightly revenue job moved to the data platform team
Backfills are paused while the Snowflake warehouse is being resized
All cloud resources are defined in Terraform with state stored in an S3 backend
Terraform changes are applied by Atlantis after a pull request is approved
Secrets are stored in AWS Secrets Manager and read at startup, never in env files
Production runs in eu-west-1; disaster recovery is in eu-central-1
Alerts page the on-call engineer through PagerDuty
Container images are scanned with Trivy before they are pushed to ECR
User prefers examples in Kotlin over Java
User wants explanations to mention trade-offs, not just the answer
User is colorblind; avoid relying on red versus green in UI suggestions
